source_text: CAPUT TRICESIMUM QUARTUM, De gubernatione Angelorum. POrrò specialis DEI gubernatio est ANGELORUM aut HOMINUM. II. Gubernatio Angelorum est, qua a DEO gubernantur tantum spiritualiter. Angelorum gubernatio hic consideranda venit, quia horum ministerio Deus varie utitur circa homines (Psal. 91:11 et 34:8; Es. 37:36; Heb. 1:14) aliasque creaturas quae homini inserviunt. III. Estque essentiae illorum conservatio, actionum directio. IV. Essentiae eorum conservatio est, qua sine propagatione aeternantur singuli. Sunt enim spiritus, adeoque incorporei, immediate producti a Deo e nihilo, ut supra cap. 26 demonstratum est, ad generandum haud constituti (Matth. 22:30). V. Actionum directio est praescriptio legis et eventus inde sequentis ordinatio.
english: CHAPTER THIRTY-FOUR. On the governance of angels.

Next, the special governance of GOD is of ANGELS or of HUMAN BEINGS. II. The governance of angels is that by which they are governed by GOD only spiritually. Their governance must be considered here because God variously uses their ministry concerning human beings (Psalm 91:11 and 34:8; Isaiah 37:36; Hebrews 1:14) and other creatures that serve humankind.

III. It is the conservation of their essence and the direction of their actions. IV. Conservation of their essence is that by which each is eternalized without propagation. For they are spirits, and so incorporeal, produced immediately by God from nothing, as shown above in chapter 26, and not constituted for generating (Matthew 22:30). V. Direction of actions is the prescription of law and the ordination of the event that follows from it.

source_text: VI. Lex illa est, qua ab iis postulatur obedientia, quantum ad substantiam eadem, quam decalogus hominibus praescribit. Sunt autem hic excipienda ea omnia quae vel humani corporis naturam, vel huius mortalis vitae conditionem respiciunt, qualia sunt multa officia secundo et quarto praecepto, multa inferiorum erga superiores puta liberorum erga parentes quinto, multa de propagatione generis septimo, quaedam de acquirendi victus ratione octavo nobis praescripta, quae ipsis haud conveniunt. Sunt autem angelorum officia ferme quintuplicia. Sunt enim 1. cantores, 2. oratores, 3. legati, 4. protectores, 5. belli duces. Primum et princeps eorum munus est, Deum semper amare et nunquam non laudare; sic amant ut ardeant Deum, sic amant ut pervigili et insopita laudis harmonia collaudent. Concentum caeli quis dormire faciet? quaerit Iobus 38:37. Aliter in caelo canunt angeli et prolixiorem faciunt suae musicae voluptatem: incipiunt et nunquam desinunt; satiant nec taedium creant. Esaias audiit et caelestis illius orarii verba descripsit (cap. 6), ubi Seraphini clamabant alter ad alterum: Sanctus, sanctus, sanctus Dominus Deus exercituum; plena est omnis terra gloria eius. Alterum angelorum munus: oratores sunt (Apoc. 8:3). Tertium: legati sunt in summi momenti negotiis. Quartum: protectores sunt (Psal. 91). Quintum: belli duces sunt, et tales ut quoties velint a parte sua stantem habeant victoriam (Exod. 23:20; Ios. 5).
english: VI. That law is that by which obedience is required of them — the same in substance as the Decalogue prescribed to human beings. Yet here must be excepted all that regards either the nature of the human body or the condition of this mortal life: many duties of the second and fourth commandments; many of inferiors toward superiors, as of children toward parents in the fifth; many concerning the propagation of the race in the seventh; and some concerning the way of gaining livelihood in the eighth — which do not suit them.

The offices of angels are roughly fivefold. They are first singers, second orators, third ambassadors, fourth protectors, fifth war-leaders. Their first and chief task is always to love God and never cease praising Him; they so love that they burn for God, and so love that with a sleepless harmony of praise they praise Him together. Who will make the concert of heaven sleep? Job asks (38:37). Otherwise in heaven the angels sing and make the pleasure of their music more lasting: they begin and never leave off; they satisfy and create no weariness. Isaiah heard and wrote the words of that heavenly oratory (chapter 6), where the Seraphim cried one to another: Holy, holy, holy is the Lord God of hosts; the whole earth is full of His glory.

Their second office: they are orators (Revelation 8:3). Third: ambassadors in affairs of highest moment. Fourth: they are protectors (Psalm 91). Fifth: they are war-leaders, and such that whenever they will they have victory standing on their side (Exodus 23:20; Joshua 5).

source_text: VII. Ordinatio eventus est praeservatio, confirmatio aut permissio lapsus et obfirmatio. VIII. Praeservatio est, qua quidam angeli a lapsu servantur. IX. Confirmatio est, qua in bono firmati sunt. X. Sunt autem multi modi quibus boni angeli circa homines operantur: 1. linguas aperiunt et eloquia divina tradunt (Es. 6:6); 2. aegrotos sanant (Ioh. 5:4); 3. fatigatos reficiunt (1 Reg. 19:7); 4. a charis vinci se sinunt (Gen. 32:28); 5. afflictos solantur (Gen. 21:17); 6. ad benefaciendum hortantur (Act. 8:26); 7. e caelo in terras commeant (Gen. 28:12; Ioh. 1:51); 8. orantes animant (Iudic. 13); 9. castos ubique ardentissime amant et propugnant (Iudith 13:20). Quaeritur cur nullus unquam sanctorum Angelorum (quod ego quidem sciam) chari hominis corpus insiderit, quod tamen transfugae Angeli saepe saepius sunt ausi. RESPONDEO: 1. Homo templum est Numini sacrum; Angeli reverentia et amore ducti principis sui conclave suo ingressu nolunt temerare. 2. Cum Deus hominis originem adeo nobilitarit admirando divinae et humanae naturae conjugio, tam nihil sibi in hominem licere volunt Angeli ut non tantum Numinis sed et hominis servos se dici toderent.
english: VII. Ordination of the event is preservation, confirmation, or permission of a fall and hardening. VIII. Preservation is that by which certain angels are kept from falling. IX. Confirmation is that by which they are made firm in the good.

X. There are many modes by which good angels work concerning human beings: they open tongues and hand on divine speech (Isaiah 6:6); they heal the sick (John 5:4); they refresh the weary (1 Kings 19:7); they allow themselves to be overcome by the dear (Genesis 32:28); they console the afflicted (Genesis 21:17); they exhort to doing good (Acts 8:26); they pass from heaven to earth (Genesis 28:12; John 1:51); they animate those who pray (Judges 13); they love and defend the chaste everywhere most ardently (Judith 13:20).

It may be asked why no holy angel (so far as I know) has ever seated himself in a dear human body, though fugitive angels have so often dared it. I answer: first, the human being is a temple sacred to the Deity; angels, led by reverence and love, refuse to invade their Princes chamber by their own entry. Second, since God so ennobled human origin by the wondrous conjunction of divine and human nature, angels will claim so little license over a human being that they endure to be called not only servants of the Deity but servants of the human as well.

source_text: XI. Sunt autem de bonis angelis eorumque gubernatione observandi canones. 1. Angelorum in bono confirmatio non fuit debitum meriti alicuius stipendium, sed gratuitum Dei liberalissimi praemium (Rom. 11:35). 2. Angeli cuique et homini et ordini inserviunt (Psal. 34:8). 3. Homo non unum duntaxat Angelum custodem, sed multos simul habet (Psal. 91:11; Matth. 18:10; Act. 12:15; Zanchius). 4. Angeli non sunt adorandi (Apoc. 19:10). 5. Aversantur Angeli quicquid vitium redolet; maxime tamen oderunt in vitiis calorem, fumum, foetorem — calorem irae et invidiae, fumum superbiae, foetorem luxuriae.
english: XI. Canons are to be observed concerning good angels and their governance. First, the confirmation of angels in the good was not a wages owed to some merit, but the free reward of most liberal God (Romans 11:35). Second, angels serve each person and each order (Psalm 34:8). Third, a human being has not only one guardian angel but many at once (Psalm 91:11; Matthew 18:10; Acts 12:15; Zanchi). Fourth, angels are not to be adored (Revelation 19:10). Fifth, angels turn away from whatever smells of vice; yet among vices they most hate heat, smoke, and stench — the heat of anger and envy, the smoke of pride, the stench of luxury.

source_text: XII. Permissio est, qua suspensa efficientia divina angeli quidam labi sinuntur. XIII. Obfirmatio est, qua lapsi negata gratia in malo firmantur. Dicuntur etiam Immundi spiritus (Luc. 11:24), spiritus nequam (1 Reg. 16:14), spiritus erroris (1 Tim. 4:1), Satan, Diabolus, serpens antiquus, draco, angeli Satanae (Apoc. 12:9), pater mendacii (Ioh. 8:44), spiritualis nequitia (Eph. 6:12), leo rugiens (1 Pet. 5:8), daemonia (Luc. 11), satyri (Lev. 17:7), pilosi (Es. 13:21; 34:14). Ratio denominationis est quia sunt spiritus a Deo quidem creati, sed qui a veritate in qua conditi erant in principio libera voluntate defecerunt, et horribiles tam Dei quam hominum adversarii facti sunt, et aeternis ad iudicium vinculis servantur (Ioh. 8:44; 2 Pet. 2:4; Iudae 6).
english: XII. Permission is that by which, with divine efficiency suspended, certain angels are allowed to fall. XIII. Hardening is that by which the fallen, grace denied, are made firm in evil.

They are also called unclean spirits (Luke 11:24), worthless spirits (1 Kings 16:14), spirits of error (1 Timothy 4:1), Satan, the Devil, the ancient serpent, the dragon, angels of Satan (Revelation 12:9), father of the lie (John 8:44), spiritual wickedness (Ephesians 6:12), roaring lion (1 Peter 5:8), demons (Luke 11), satyrs (Leviticus 17:7), hairy ones (Isaiah 13:21; 34:14). The reason for the naming is that they are spirits created by God indeed, but who by free will fell away at the beginning from the truth in which they were made, and became horrible adversaries of both God and human beings, and are kept in eternal chains for judgment (John 8:44; 2 Peter 2:4; Jude 6).

source_text: XIV. Sunt autem de iis notandi canones. 1. Diabolus malus fuit ab initio non creationis, sed defectionis (Augustinus; Thomas; Zanchius). 2. Impii sunt filii Diaboli non respectu substantiae suae, sed intuitu accidentis malitiae. 3. Diabolus primus author est et fons peccati, malitiae tum in sua ipsius natura tum in genere humano (Ioh. 8:44; 1 Ioh. 3:8). 4. Angeli lapsi retinuerunt quidem substantiam suam cum intellectu et voluntate, magnaque insuper potentia, sed omnibus istis duntaxat ad malum feruntur. 5. Diabolus intellectu, voluntate, potentia viribusque suis omnibus abutitur non solum ad malitiam suam propagandam, sed et regnum Dei exstirpandum. 6. Diabolus hominum cogitationes non callet nisi per externa signa et probabiliter, aut impuras quas ipse suggerit. 7. Magna Satanae potentia est, sed sub Dei omnipotentia. 8. Diabolus facere potest mirabilia, non autem vera et proprie dicta miracula. 9. Diabolus facit quod potest, Deo permittente; quod potest, non facit, Deo prohibente. 10. Nemo homo suis viribus Diabolum repellere eique resistere potest; sed Dei solius gratia et potentia est eum superare, et a laqueis ipsius hominem resipiscentem et credentem explicare.
english: XIV. Canons are to be noted concerning them. First, the Devil was evil from the beginning not of creation but of defection (Augustine; Thomas; Zanchi). Second, the impious are children of the Devil not with respect to their substance but in view of the accident of malice. Third, the Devil is the first author and fountain of sin — of malice both in his own nature and in the human race (John 8:44; 1 John 3:8). Fourth, fallen angels retained their substance with intellect and will, and great power besides, but by all these they are borne only to evil. Fifth, the Devil abuses intellect, will, power, and all his forces not only to propagate his malice but also to root out Gods kingdom.

Sixth, the Devil does not know human thoughts except through outward signs and probably, or impure ones that he himself suggests. Seventh, Satans power is great, but under Gods omnipotence. Eighth, the Devil can do wonders, but not true and properly so-called miracles. Ninth, the Devil does what he can when God permits; what he can, he does not do when God forbids. Tenth, no human being by his own powers can drive back the Devil and resist him; it is Gods grace and power alone to overcome him and to free the repentant and believing human being from his snares.
